name: What size drywall holes can be repaired versus requiring panel replacement?

mainEntity.name: What size drywall holes can be repaired versus requiring panel replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Small holes, typically up to 4-6 inches in diameter, can often be repaired using a patch kit, spackle, and sanding. For holes larger than this, especially those with significant damage to the surrounding drywall or stud, a section of the drywall panel may need to be cut out and replaced. The extent of the damage and the integrity of the wall determine whether a repair or replacement is more appropriate. Professional assessment ensures the most durable and seamless result.
acceptedAnswer.description: Small holes (up to 4-6 inches) are typically patched, while larger holes often require replacing a section of the drywall panel.
